MODULE 8: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-2 INTO 2-ON-2 HALF-COURT

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Assign players to each basket. With low numbers, have two teams of three players at each basket. With high numbers, have five teams of three players at each basket. Begin by playing 3-on-2, where the offense must score a 3PT shot or a lay-up in 12 seconds. After a shot or turnover occurs, the player who was last in possession of the ball must track the ball down. They will then pass it into the other two offensive players, who play 2-on-2 against the defenders. Once this second repetition is complete, the activity resets with new teams in and ready to begin with the first repetition of 3-on-2.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Making quick decisions to make the advantage greater
- Finding a way to get to the rim for the most efficient shot

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out outside the 3PT line). If they are still inside after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Simply convert the 3-on-2 advantage which exists.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players understand the last player to touch the ball on offense is out for the 2-on-2.
- Ensure that the next group is primed and ready to rotate in.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Can you find the ROB shot?"

Load for younger players

MODULE 8: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-2 ADVANCE THE BALL

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets (cut the court along rim line to create two playing spaces per basket)

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

The offense and defense must stay in half of the full-court area, playing from sideline to rim line. Cones may be used to mark out the rim line. The offense has to progress the ball from one baseline to the other baseline, without being allowed to pass forward. The offense can therefore only dribble or pass laterally or backwards ('rugby' load). The defense can do anything they want to disrupt the offense, including trapping. If the defense steals the ball, they must immediately attempt to score a 'touchdown' with the same rules. After a 'touchdown' has been scored, change teams.

#### SCORING

Offensive players get 1 point for 'touchdown'.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space and keeping advantage
- Disruptive defense

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Allow forwards passes, but offense get 2 points if they score the 'touchdown' without passing ahead.
- Play until a score using the 'rugby' load.
- Allow two forwards passes each possession.
- Play the same game 3-on-3 using the whole full-court area (instead of staying in half the space).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Officiate the 'rugby' load.
- Encourage the defense to explore disruptive solutions such as trapping.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How could you force the offense into a turnover?"
- "Offensively, how can you win this game without passing ahead"?

MODULE 8: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

I-ON-I+I DRIVE AND KICK

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players will work in groups of three or four. An offensive player will start in any 5-out spacing location, with another teammate in any other spot. The offense will begin with the defender on their hip, outside the 3PT line. The moment they drive the ball, the live 1-on-1 begins and the defense is allowed to steal the ball. However, the offense must enter the paint with the drive and pass the ball to their teammate before they are allowed to score. After passing the ball, they must re-space back out to the perimeter. From here, they must do whatever they can to get open to receive the pass back from their teammate to play 1-on-1.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The +1 stands inside the mid-range to create an easier pass. Once they receive the kick-out pass, the defender must tag them with one hand before they can close back out to the offensive player for the 1-on-1.
- The offensive player only passes if the +1 shows both hands. If the +1 does not show both hands, they can score off the first drive. If the +1 makes a connection, they must re-space and play the 1-on-1 from there.
- Play 2-on-1 where either player can score after the kick-out.
- Play 2-on-2 where the offense is allowed to score on the first drive if they are not stopped.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Help players identify the 5-out spacing spots.
- Reinforce the 'lava' load.
- Ensure players re-space and explore different ways to get open. The +1 can run dribble hand-offs/set picks to help the player get open.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space and keeping advantage
- Creative finishing

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where should you re-space to?"
- "How could you help the offensive player score?" (to the facilitator)

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-3 HALF-COURT CONTINUOUS

20 MIN
BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of three. Make sure each basket has a minimum of three teams and a maximum of six. Teams play half-court 3-on-3 with additional teams waiting at the baseline. When an offensive team scores, the defense sprints off while a new defensive team comes on from the baseline. The new defense must all touch the 3PT line prior to matching up and playing defense. At the same time, all offensive players must advance the ball and touch the half-court line before they begin 3-on-3 against the new team.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Beating initial defense and reading second and third levels of help defense
- Identifying the open player

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "What is the 'lava' load teaching?"
- "Where is the space?"
- "What are ways to speed up and take advantage of your transition?"

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, inside the paint is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Escape the lava. After a pass or off-ball cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out outside the 3PT line). If they are still inside after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Players can only create an advantage through a static 1-on-1 where the ball-handler creates an advantage by looking to create through a dribble move from the perimeter, or through a post-up. Teammates should maintain spacing (inside the 3PT line is lava), ready to receive the ball.
- 'Inside the 3PT line is lava' load applies but post-ups are allowed.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure the players keep and communicate score.
- Make sure players start from different angles and locations.
- Remind players to transition quickly and take advantage after a score (offense touch half-court, defense touch 3PT line).

MODULE 8: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

24 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of 5 players, based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of 5 teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, instead of using full-courts, half-courts can be used. Teams play to 3 baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get 1 point. The losing team will rotate off while the next team waiting rotates on. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

#### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

#### KEY WORDS

- "How can you get the most efficient shot?"
- "How can we help teammates to emphasize continuous ball pressure?"
- "What can you do to space the floor effectively?"

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Pass and cut is a turnover: create an advantage through static 1-on-1.
- Double teams that lead to turnovers result in an extra 3 points.
- No ball pressure results in the defensive team losing 1 point and the offense regaining possession on the sideline.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.

Load for younger players
